rationale: Classic mutable default argument trap. The empty list `notes=[]` is created once at function definition time and shared across all calls that don't provide an explicit `notes` argument. Subsequent calls without providing `notes` will keep appending to the same list object, accumulating notes across invocations instead of creating a fresh list each time. This matches the 'known_trap' flavor (mutable default argument) and 'trivial' severity (affects only the return value of calls using the default, no persistent storage corruption).
